utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just a preliminary matter. Your Honours, Friday I made an oral motion to remove VG-145 from the Prosecution witness list for its rebuttal case. The events are recent, and I will not recount them other than to say I took this step when the witness, just before testifying, demanded that he and his family be relocated to a different country. The Chamber granted my application, I was informed last evening that VG-145 initiated contact with our Sarajevo field office late yesterday to express his regret about his conduct and to express his willingness to come before the Chamber and testify honestly and without any preconditions about what he knows about this case. Given these recent events, I think I would be remiss if I did not did anything other than to suggest to the Chamber that it must approach his evidence with caution. He is someone who has sought personal gain and advantage from these proceedings. It is for these very qualities that I submit he was first approached with a proposal to give purgered testimony. Having said that I would also be remiss if I did not do everything within my power to bring all reliable evidence before the Chamber to place it in the best position to fairly and justly adjudicate this case. Despite the despicable conduct of VG-145 there is evidence that he has to give which is reliable. The map he says was drawn by Milan Lukic has been examined by a handwriting expert who says that it probably was, in fact, drawn by Milan Lukic. He also provided a blank pro forma statement weeks before a completed version of that statement was passed to the Prosecution within the full view of the Bench. A meeting he had with MLD1 is corroborated with footage from a security camera. VG-145's change of mind and willingness to now come before the Chamber and subject him stove rigorous examination and cross-examination ensures that the Chamber will be placed in a position to make its own careful assessment of him, and it ensures that the rights of Milan Lukic to confront him and test the serious allegations he makes. For reasons that will be fully set forth in the final trial brief, the different alibis of Milan Lukic are actually interconnected. It is my view that if the Chamber credits his evidence related to the map and the pro forma statement, which I believe it can do because the reliability of that evidence does not wholly depend on the credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I don't think there's any need to address us on how his evidence is to be treated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. So Your Honour, I'm asking leave to re-add VG-1 45 to the Prosecution list in its rebuttal case. I have asked a member of my staff to be in contact with VWS to make a preliminary plans so that to avoid any delay should the Chamber grant this application. Of course, I will not -- I've asked him to allow him to board any plane until the Chamber makes a decision on my request. So I ask the Chamber to give serious consideration to re-adding VG-145.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One very major objection we would is to that is as Your Honours know, I'm here solo. Mr. Alarid who had prepared for VG-145 when he was initially scheduled to testify is not here, will not be here this week at all as Your Honours already know from the filings we've already done. Due to the history of the case, obviously we decided that it would be improper for me to cross-examine this witness based upon the allegations this witness has made. Therefore, we are in a position that if he is to be brought -- if the Trial Chamber is going to consider this application, by the Prosecution, we have no one here available to cross-examine him. And that would be very unfair and unjust to the Defence particularly in light of the evidence that has been led as to this individual and how we have shed light on his -- on the nature of his allegations to the point that Your Honours have seen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, we'll give our decision within an hour or two. Please call the next witness, I think it's a Court witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I wonder if I could be heard as a preliminary matter, Your Honours, while the witness is being brought in. Now, this witness, Mr. Kurspahic has been recalled to be asked questions about the victims of the Pionirska fire. Just in the event that it might be suggested by the Defence in the event, Your Honours, that it might be suggested by the Defence that the information provided by Mr. Kurspahic in a recent phone call is all new material, I should just like to point out the following: He testified in the Mitar Vasiljevic trial in 2001, and much of the information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, I have developed the practice that interventions of the kind that you are making now should be made during the course of the evidence and not before, when it arises, and I'd prefer if you would wait until it comes up in during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason that I was raising it now, it was effectively a prelude to asking that there be no leading questions from counsel because of the situation of the information that they have available. Just to save time in due course me standing up and objecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, well, I will make that clear. In any event, that's the rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, he is being recalled for the cross-examination by the Defence, so I'm entitled to lead him. He was a Prosecution witness. When new information developed, we asked to recall him, so he is still essentially being recalled for cross-examination. That is the only reason we brought him here. We've already had him testify once. We have want to ask him about this new information that he has since he testified here.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is the reason that I started out on this brief introduction. The Defence have had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He is a Chamber witness. He is a Chamber witness, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, what I'm trying to say, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think either party may put any questions to him. Either party. He is a witness of the Court, and I will allow either party to put any questions to him whether it is seen as examination-in-chief or as leading. He is properly a Chamber witness and therefore liable to be questioned by either party. Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. I think it's appropriate for the Defence to begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And for purposes of the protection of other witnesses who have been subjected to protective measures, one moment, I forgot one, I would like to have a pseudonym sheet before the witness so he can know which witness I'm referring to when I use the pseudonyms as these proceedings are being led in open question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, first of all, let me introduce myself. My name is Dan Ivetic, and I'm one of the attorneys for the Defence of Milan Lukic, and certain revelations have happened since the last time you were here which we were trying to make sense of and that's why we are here to help us understand that new evidence. Now, while we are waiting for the sheet to reach you, sir, first of all, am I correct that you are not seeking protective measures, and I can refer to you by name?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And I understand we can take a copy of the pseudonym sheet, so I will ask you my preliminary questions; first of all, sir, has anyone met with you to prepare or proof you for your testimony prior to today for this testimony?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sir, did you, in fact, have a telephone discussion with the Office of the Prosecution within the last several months?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us about each and every telephone conversation you've had with staff from the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal in the past several months?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: It only happened once and it was a brief conversation. I cannot recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we've been provided with information from the Office of the Prosecution that, in fact, on March -- on or about March the 4th of 2009, they had a telephonic discussion with you. Does that refresh your recollection as to when the conversation would have been had between you and the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Most probably it was on that day. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Sir, I see that the pseudonym sheet has made its way to you. You see there pseudonyms for several, I believe it is maybe, five or six named persons, I believe all those persons are known to you. I would ask for their protection that we honour their protective measures and we use their pseudonyms there instead of their names. So, sir, you can keep that sheet in front of you so that you can refer to it if need be. Now, if we can return to this telephone call with the Office of the Prosecutor. Do you recall or was it represented to you who from the Office of the Prosecutor was on the phone with you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know who the interpreter was, although they introduced themselves. I think there was a Mr. Steven [phoen]who was there, and a female interpreter interpreting his words. I wasn't very interested in who was representing whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough, sir. Now, when they called you, did they tell you the subject matter or reason for which they were calling?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I didn't understand it fully well. I think they said that there might be a need for me to appear before the Court again and that some things may need clarification. I said that if need be, I'm prepared to appear again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the course of that telephone conversation with the Office of the Prosecutor was it made known to you that there had been a recent filing made by the Defence of Milan Lukic alleging problems with the list of victims, and that certain victims were alleged to be alive?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: It was precisely about the list and the names of individuals. That's why I'm here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, let me take a step backwards first. Are you familiar with the indictment handed down by this Tribunal against Milan Lukic, including the Annex A, which would be the annex of alleged victims from the Pionirska Street alleged incident?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you have an opportunity to review that Annex A list of victims prior to the time that you testified in this Tribunal last time?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I have that list from a previous hearing in the case of Mitar Vasiljevic. I think some of the names have been corrected. I don't know where the mistake occurred though. When it took place, people were uncertain who survived, who did not. Later on some people resurfaced alive. I have a list, and I can go name by name here before the Court with all the names and the houses where people lived. I have it all with me, and if necessary, I can inform the Bench. Also I can show you the whole list, and I believe it to be authentic and precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, I appreciate your comments. Now, before we get to all that, I'd look to ask you, since you have testified, I believe, you've testified in this case, did you also testify previously in one of the other cases of the Tribunal about the alleged incident at Pionirska?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In the case of Mitar Vasiljevic. During the critical period, he was near the building, and I provided a statement against Mitar Vasiljevic basically; and I also, I think, on the 8th of August last year, I gave a statement against Milan and Sredoje. This would be my third time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And you would agree with me that on the two prior occasion that is you testified before this Tribunal, you had an opportunity to correct any information on that list of victims from the Annex A of the indictment if you had known that such information was incorrect?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, just to finish up on that point that we started on before the digression. In fact, I believe when you testified here the last time you had, in fact, made some corrections or clarifications by way of a proofing statement with Mr. Stevan Cole, the Office of the Prosecution done just before you testified here that day; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, the problem that we have or the question that we have I guess is related to you, I should say, is that with respect to the victims, the named victims in Annex A of the indictment, we'd like to know how it is possible that between 1992, and for instance when you testified last here at the Tribunal, you did not know of the corrections that you've now given most recently on or about March the 4th of 2009, that were only -- it would seem to an outside observer those corrections were only made after the filing by the Milan Lukic Defence bringing into question the list, so I would like to know when you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: My learned friend is doing this in a global way, in other words suggesting that they are all in the same category, and they are not. And in fairness to the witness, they should be put individually rather than the global fashion because the witness made a number of corrections, for example, in his testimony during the Vasiljevic trial and it's not all new. So my objection is that this should be done in an individual fashion rather than a global fashion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, put them individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honours. If we can call up then 1D22-900.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, what is coming up on a screen is a document that was disclosed to the Defence by the Prosecution that purports to record or chronicle the clarifications resulting from your March 4th, 2009 telephonic discussion of a member of the Office of the Prosecution although this document does not identify with whom you had the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And to allay the fears of the Prosecution, this ought to be the redacted version, I believe. Let me just double-check, though. So we should probably not publish it until the full page comes up, so I can see whether it is the redacted or the unredacted. If you just scroll down, I'll find out right away. This is the unredacted, so this actually should not be published, but it will help us to have the witness have the full information before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, looking at this list, I'd first like to go through Jasmina Delija. When is the first time that you remembered she is actually the same person as Jasmina or Mina Kurspahic as she is placed in the annex of victims?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you can see from the note before the witness that counsel is misrepresenting the information that's there. And I don't know whether the witness can read English, but perhaps the contents of the -- in fairness, the contents of the actual notes should be put to him rather than paraphrasing the way counsel is at the moment, which seems to be misrepresenting what is there. You can see, Your Honour, that that note, in fact, just gives a maiden name, not as the way counsel has described it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me try a different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, perhaps you and I can understand ourselves better if I say it this way, Jasmina Kurspahic was also known as Mina Kurspahic; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: May I say something? Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Jasmina Kurspahic known as Mina Kurspahic became married and her name was then Jasmina Delija; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So would you agree with me that when you say, and I'll put to you what the notes from your telephonic discussions say: The maiden name of Jasmina Delija was Kurspahic; am I correct in understanding that to mean that Jasmina Delija and Mina Kurspahic are the same person, sir?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. What is there to be disputed?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: There's no other Jasmina on the list. No other Jasmina Kurspahic. I came before the Tribunal with this document specifying the names and families from A to Z. I can stay here for five days, if we need to clarify each and every fact. Ask me whatever you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you everything, and I will hopefully get to do that. But you have to cooperate with me. I will present you everything, you can answer and the other side will have an opportunity to ask if I've forgotten anything. Now, the question I have for you, sir, is with respect to the individual we have just mentioned, you've indicated there is no other; but, sir, the same person appears as number 43 on the list and as number 4 on the list, Jasmina Delija, Mina Kurspahic. Now, I'd like to ask you: Did you know of this error on the list prior to your testimony last time before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, my learned friends is misrepresenting what is in the indictment, what is in the note, and is with respect, I think the witness is being misled. What counsel is trying to do is to get this witness to confirm that it's the same person under two different names on the Annex A; but it hasn't been made clear to the witness with respect by the nature of the questions. Now, I think the first thing that needs to be made clear to the witness is that counsel is referring to names on the annex to the indictment, and the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I've stated at least five times, Your Honour, and Mr. Cole had adequate opportunity to do his examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm objecting to counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, let me hear Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, I've lost my train of thought now, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Don't allow Mr. Ivetic to have that effect on you, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: In fairness to the witness if counsel is suggesting that two persons in Annex A are the same person, he should put that to the witness without beating around so the witness can address that particularly, sir, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I'll have to back up to see the question that was posed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, on the list, that is to say on Annex A from the second amended indictment against Milan Lukic, at position number 4 we have a Jasmina Delija, and at position number 43 we have a Mina Kurspahic; and I'd like to ask you given your knowledge of the names and the individuals, would you agree with me that this is the same person listed twice?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Now, is that important at all, whether one person was burnt, 20 people burnt, 50 people burnt. Mr. President, may I be allowed to say this, you are tying me to a detail here. The fact of the matter is that the young girl married, changed her surname, her nickname is Mina and her real name is Jasmina, so where is the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The problem is when witnesses come here and testify under oath we expect that the information is true and correct, sir, and that is what we are trying to ascertain with respect to the evidence that has been led by the Prosecution what evidence is true and correct and what is not. And that's what we are here to help us with your knowledge, sir, and I would beg your indulgence and your patience because we will go through all of your clarifications, and I will give you an ample opportunity to explain all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic, he has answered, please proceed, remember you have half an hour, no more. The same applies to Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The same applies to Mr. Cole unless I give you more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, he is not a rebuttal witness. All right. I will try and proceed through it, Your Honours. As you can see it's difficult though with the objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, okay, we've done that one. Did you know about this error on Annex A of the indictment prior to your testimony last time?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I didn't know. Had I known, I would have put it right, so what is the problem now? I didn't add to the list those 22 names that I could have, I'm here to clear things up, to tell you what the facts were so that we can establish the truth, the real truth. That is why I am here today, sir. Now I allow you to ask me precisely the questions you want me to answer. I've been engaged in matters like this. I've done jobs like this for 20 years, so I know what all this is about but go ahead, ask me precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, I've been asking you precisely. And let's move along precisely. Now, if we look at item D on your list, you state -- pardon me, the Prosecution represents as to your statement: "He believes that Aner Kurspahic, son of Latifa Kurspahic is alive and in Austria." Now --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, and he is not on the list. He is not on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, he is number 15 on the list. He is on the list. Let me finish my questions, and we'll get through this much easier. Now, you identify this as the son of Latifa Kurspahic, are we to assume from this information that you know Latifa Kurspahic is alive?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, she is alive, living in Austria, has two daughters. She is living in Austria with her two daughters in Austria. What more do you want to know?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now with respect to Meva Kurspahic, at H on your list; isn't it correct that this is the wife of Hasan, the mother Omer, and the grandmother of Aner?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I haven't got that list, what list are you look at, sir, because I don't have a list like that, and I never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The one in front of you.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: You are asking me some things that are aren't linked to this trial. You can't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me read to you what the Office of the Prosecution says what you told them, and we'll see whether it's a left thing or not. And I quote, "He," meaning you, "is aware of Meva Kurspahic, mother of Omer and Fikret, who is now dead, but whom he believes was not killed in the Pionirska fire." Now do we understand each other about which Meva we are talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, and she wasn't burnt in the fire. She died in Sarajevo and was buried after that. So where is this Meva on the list? Show me. I've never seen that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, sir, she is number 42 on the list. Now, sir, given what you've testified about here today now as to these individuals, would you agree with me that we can take off of the list of victims Meva, Latifa --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- her daughters. Wait until I finish, sir.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you give us the numbers, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Actually, no, I can't, Your Honours, because of the duplication of names on the list there is a submission we've filed pursuant to the sworn testimony of CW1, protected witness CW1, which clarifies her testimony; so I would refer to that submission as to the names of persons who follow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you would agree with me that that entire family did not perish in Pionirska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you happen to be at Meva Kurspahic's funeral that occurred in the past five years in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, when or how long have you known that the direct family of Omer Kurspahic did not perish in Pionirska? Was it before either of the two times you testified here previously?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I wonder, Your Honour, if we could just be clear when we talk about a whole family, it's a rather indistinct expression. If we could know exactly which members he is referring to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic, that's a fair question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why don't you just name the persons in the family that you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, for those persons who are not familiar with the names of the various Kurspahic family, I will have to go through all of them, would you agree with me that the family of Omer Kurspahic, that is to say his wife, Lejla; his two daughters; his son, Aner; his mother, Meva; his father, Hasan were not at Koritnik at the time of the alleged Pionirska fire and, therefore, did not perish in the fire as is alleged in the indictment and in the list of victims?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: That's right, they weren't, but I haven't got the list, may I take a look at the list on the screen and see who compiled the list? The Prosecution's here. Could I have the list, could they show me the list or the Trial Chamber, so that I can see the list because you keep asking me the number based on the list and I don't have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are trying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, just a minute, please. You will be shown the list as it appears in the annex.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately I only have a clean English version of the same, but I believe the names should be able to be read, they are the same in B/C/S, in English, the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, the question I had for you was with respect to this family --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just let him look at the list for a minute or two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Now, tell me what number Aner is under and Meva? I'm asking the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Aner is number 15 on the list.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you are being asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Aner is number 15 on the list.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Aner, I have never seen this list before. It's not something I had, and I certainly didn't write it. And the truth is, that he wasn't there, but Milan Lukic took him out of the car with his father and uncle and Milan took him away, straightaway. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Before we begin, before we began I asked you if you were familiar with the indictment and Annex A the list of victims in the indictment and whether you had reviewed the same prior to testifying, sir. And you had answered in the affirmative. That is a public document. It's a document that was published. It is a document that we are defending in this case. This is what the Prosecution provided us as to the victims of the alleged incident, and I'd like to go through with you, sir.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: This is a mistake that the Prosecution made and failed to put right on time. But I stand by everything I've said here. It is correct and truthful, and I'm here to establish the truth and I have absolutely no reason to add anything or take anything away, add a name or subtract a name. That's in nobody's interest. It's not in the interests of this Tribunal or the Defence or anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With all deference to you I'm trying not to interrupt you, sir, but we have a limited time. And we have a long way to go. And I would ask you to look at the list that has now been provided for you, and you ask me to identify where persons are listed. I already told you about Aner. We have Latifa at 36; Lejla at 37; we have 42, Meva; we've had some evidence that 38, Majda, might be the other daughter of Latifa; we have Hasan at number 26. We have --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Hasan disappeared. Hasan went missing. There are two Hasans: Hasan Kurspahic, Hajra's son, and this is Alija's son, Fikret Alija.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Before we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, let's get some order into it. Let's start with what you are going to put to him those names on the list that you say should not be there, you are starting first with 15, Aner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm starting by the categories of his clarifications, Your Honour, that are in the document on the screen right now. I don't know necessarily that they were all be on the list to take off, that's why I'm asking the gentleman what he knew. What I'm more concerned about is when did he find out this information because again we've had witnesses come here and testify and affirm the very same annex on multiple occasions. And now after we do some investigations, we find out that they have known that persons shouldn't be on the list. That is what the real crux of our submission is to find out when they knew this information, and whether, therefore, the testimony that they gave at this Tribunal is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have already asked him that, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to this particular family, I have asked and he has not answered. I've asked about the Jasmina Delija, and he has answered. So I'm going through all his clarifications to find out exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But go through them one by one, and let's proceed that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where are you now?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm right now going to I'm at D on his list, which is where we started talking about Aner Kurspahic, the family, the direct family of Omer Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, when did you know that that family was not a family that had been in Koritnik at the time of the alleged Pionirska incident and, therefore, could not have been alleged at the alleged Pionirska incident? When did you know that, sir?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Afterwards when Hasan and Meva returned from Austria was it in 1997 thereabouts when I met Hasan, and he has died since. I didn't know before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So sometime in 1997. Now, if I can ask you about the individuals --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, so don't insist on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me clarify to you. Was it before you testified here, sir?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Afterwards. After the first time. I don't know, I really don't know, and this is the first time that I'm looking at this list here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question. You say that Meva and Hasan returned from Austria, am I correct that they resided in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, afterwards, 1997 or 1998 when they returned. They lived in Sarajevo. They died in Sarajevo, both of them, and were buried in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the names on the pseudonym sheet now, sir, that is VG-18, VG-78, VG-84, and VG-13, do you know if any of those other relatives or persons of yours had contact with and knew of the fact that this family had not been in Koritnik and had not been at the Pionirska incident?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know whether they know that. I really couldn't say because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Did you attend any funerals for either Meva or Hasan?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I've already said where I was, yes, at both funerals. They are relatives of mine, yes, I did attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. What about VG-18, VG-78, VG-84, and VG-13, were they at either of those funerals, sir?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move along. Now, with respect to these clarifications that you gave to the Office of the Prosecution on the 4th of March, 2009, have you talked with VG-18, VG-78, VG-84, or VG-31 [sic] about those clarifications and corrections?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't do anything. They are separate, I don't know when they came, when they were here. I don't know that. I know when I was here and what I said, and I'm here to confirm everything that I've already said. You can ask me everything from A to Z, one by one, name and surname and that's how you'll get the exact names, the first and last names, and I'll state them before this Trial Chamber. One by one from A to Z from 1 the first number to whatever the last number is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Staying with VG-18, VG-78, VG-84 and VG-31 [sic] did you have occasion to see them at a protest organised by Bakira Hasecic in the village of Koritnik on or about March the 9th, 2009?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: What date did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On or about March 9th?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour. I understand the purpose this witness is here is to discuss the victims and the list of names on the schedule. Now, the Defence had ample opportunity when Mr. Kurspahic was here last time in September to cross-examine, and they did cross-examine; but they didn't ask anything about victims. I'm going to suggest, Your Honour, that we don't have a lot of time, that they confine their cross-examination now to the matters that Your Honours have pointed to, the matters that have been raised in the note that's before the witness, rather than digressing on to other witnesses. We'll be here all day, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I thought that truth finding was the main job of this Tribunal, and I, for one, am appalled by the Office of the Prosecution tactics in this case with respect to the major element of this indictment that the list of victims is finding out to have persons that did not perish, or are alive. That is an affront to this system, and I don't know what the Prosecution is afraid of, but I want to find out the truth of all of this and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- ask my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you said there were two -- first of all, question I wanted to ask you before, with respect to VG-18, VG-78, VG-84, and/or VG-31 [sic], did you have contact with any of them at a protest, organised by Bakira Hasecic of the associating of women victims of war held in the village of Koritnik, in the municipality of Visegrad on or about the 9th of March, 2009, less than one month ago?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I was in Koritnik, sir. I was in my village Koritnik from where these victims were from on the 8th of April, and we had all survived, all those who had survived were there; and all the locals of Koritnik were in the village and we commemorated that day at each individual house. And I'd like to ask the President of this Tribunal to take a look at this piece of paper where we were: Every house is marked here, the family, the individuals, the first and last names, and the number of people who died in the house; so if you need this I'll help you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I really must insist that you answer my question. Did you have contact with VG-18, VG-78, VG-84, and/or VG-13 when you were in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I'm not hiding anything. They are my relatives. Yes, I have contact with them all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you at that time talk with them about clarifications that needed to be made, correction that needed to be made, persons that were wrongfully on the list of victims, sir? Did you have conversations with them at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No, and I don't think they know about it either. I can guarantee with my life, they don't know about this list. I know that I've never seen this list before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, they were present, at least some of them were presented, with this list and affirmed it on behalf of the Prosecution; and I have evidence from another witness that, in fact, they were present at some of the funerals and, therefore, know precisely what the persons we've already talked about that they are alive and not on the list, sir; so I take umbrance [sic] with that assertion that is contrary to the evidence. But let me please focus us --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: What, which?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: My learned friend is giving evidence from where he stands at the bar, and I would just ask that he put proper questions to the witness and treat the witness with respect, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic. No comments, just proceed with the questions and we'll get on more quicker.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It's very clear I've been trying to treat the witness with the utmost of respect and not trying to interrupt him, but that is very serious matter and very serious consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, you mentioned that Hasan disappeared and went missing and we are talking now about Alija's son.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Never said that. That's not what it says. Hasan Kurspahic, Hajra's son, he was the one. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: He wasn't at Pionirska either, is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: He was, and he disappeared. He was burnt, Hajra's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... item number C on your list, sir. I'm going to read it to you, it says one of his sisters who perished in the Pionirska fire was known by the name of Hana Kurspahic and also Hasiba Kurspahic. Is that a correction you made with the Prosecution on or about the 4th of March, 2009?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that mis-characterizes what is on the document. I heard my learned friends say correction, now, that's hardly a correction giving another name that a person is known by, so I would object to it being characterized that way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hana Kurspahic, they call her Hana; but her real name is Hasiba, it's the same person, and it's my sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would VG-18, VG-78, VG-13, VG-84, would they all know about this same name being applied to the same person?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether they know her real name. Hasiba is her real name, Hana is what we called her, everybody called her Hana. But Hasiba is her real name, her full name, and she was always called Hana.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, sir, I really must insist, we don't have all the time in the world. I need to have answers to my very precise questions. I've been trying very hard to be very precise. To the extent that Hana and Hasiba are both listed as separate persons on the index in the indictment at numbers 25 and 27, I believe, would you agree with me that that is an error on the list in the indictment and therefore one of those names is a duplicate?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours, there may be many persons with the same name as in the case of Hana, and I think in fairness that should be part of the proposition put to him. This witness is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's amazing I have to do the work of the Prosecution to investigate this case. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. We want to move ahead as quickly as possible. What was the last question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The last question was if numbers 25 and 27 on the list are both Hana and Hasiba reflected as separate individuals would you agree with me they are the same person and one is a duplicate of the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's one person. One in the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we look at item number F on your sheet that the Prosecution gave to me it says, and I'll read it for you so you can have it in your language: Hasnija Kurspahic is possibly the same person as Pasana or Pasija Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Pasija is the real name. She is Hasnija's mother. I don't know what people are called, but I know that Pasija is her real name.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To the extent that number 28 on the list in the indictment is Hasnija and number 50 on the list is Pasana or Pasija would you agree with me then that that is the same person and duplicate and an error on the list of alleged victims from Pionirska?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it's just Pasija. That's it. So it's one person here too.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Would that be something that would be commonly known so that VG-18, VG-78, VG-84, and VG-13 ought to also know that Hasnija is the same person as Pasija?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you are actually asking me, why you are asking me about them. You had an opportunity of asking them so don't ask me about them otherwise I'm not going to say anything. You had your chance if they were here in court then you could have talked to them about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, please listen to me. Please listen to me carefully.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I want you to answer the questions that counsel puts to you. If any question is out of order, I will stop him. That's my job. Now, let's go ahead. And let's -- how much longer do you have, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At this point Your Honour, I don't even know I've been thrown off with simple questions that take long to answer, and there's objections, I would hope to finish within the first session is my original estimate; but I see now that we are already one hour and ten minutes into it, and I'm approximately halfway through my list of questions, so -- list of areas, I should say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we can shorten this, if this witness isn't asked what other people know, it's not a proper area of cross-examination, the witness, what other people know or might know and it can shorten things in any event. And it seems that my learned friend is going back to that issue time and again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I can make a representation on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't wants to hear you on it. Just proceed with the questioning. Let's end this examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well then I would ask you to reconsider your order denying us to bring back the other VG-18, VG-78, VG-84, VG-13, Your Honours. This is the only witness that we represent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead with the questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would that be something that would be commonly known that VG-18, VG-78, VG-8,4 and VG-13 also should know that Hasnija is the same person as Pasija?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Well, I guess they should know, they lived in the same village. Pasija had a daughter by the name of Hasnija. She did not die in the fire. That's not the same person. Hasnija is Pasija's daughter. Hasnija got killed and Pasija was not killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Item G on your list of clarifications as represented by the Office of the Prosecution says: "He is aware of another Ismeta Kurspahic, but he believes she lives in Bihac, and has always lived there." The question I have for you is would you agree with me to your knowledge there are only two Ismeta Kurspahic's: One who has always lived in Bihac, and, therefore, was not in Visegrad in 1992; and the one who was in Visegrad and is listed as an alleged victim in Annex A of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, insofar as we have had -- so far as we have had a document in this case, the Visegrad Health Centre's log-books for the record that would be ERN 0545-2135, the second page of that would be 0545-2136. We have an entry for the 18th of June for a Ismeta Kurspahic. If that document is accurate, sir, would you then agree with me that the Ismeta Kurspahic listed as having perished in the Pionirska fire may well have not perished in that alleged incident?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: She was killed. That is correct. It is incorrect that she reported down there in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we have a document that states that is a person by the name of Ismeta Kurspahic was treated at the Visegrad health --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see Mr. Cole on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Sir, counsel has his answer. He is repeating the question, it seems, to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I may complete my question since I was not repeating the answer. Now, we have a document that states that a person by the name of Ismeta Kurspahic was treated at the Visegrad Health Centre, June 18th of 1992; would you agree with me that apart from the Ismeta Kurspahic that you say was killed in the fire on the 14th of June, there are no other persons with that name in Visegrad who could have applied to the Visegrad Health Centre? And I'm told the document is 1D22-0898 if it is something that is required to be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: There is no other Ismeta. The one in Bihac was not there. She was not in the census of 1991 in Visegrad because she resided in Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- well, we have the document coming up but he has answered the question so I don't think we need it, although -- well, I guess at this time I would tender this as the next available 1D exhibit to get that out of the way, the selected pages from the log-book of the Visegrad Health Centre. I don't know whether we have a translation so perhaps it should be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Marked for identity.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D225, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can go back to the last document which was the 1D --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sir, I'm asking questions here and, we'll get through this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, that's correct. What is it that you wish to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's only a first and last name. There's no date of birth, no father's name or anything else on the list. This is a fictitious list that I can draw up or you. In the former Yugoslavia especially in the area of Visegrad, you can get any documents in exchange for money, and I stand by what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The Prosecution's Annex A listing the alleged victims for the Pionirska Street incident also does not have father's last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I have a question for you, you've just told us some very interesting evidence. Sir, sir, listen to me, please.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Do you want me to help you or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You've given us some very important evidence. The Prosecution's Annex A to the indictment also does not have JMBG numbers, does not have father's name, does not have date of birth; are you testifying now that the Prosecution's list was procured by payments and is a false document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I'm not allowing that. Don't answer that question. Just proceed -- do not answer that question. Do not answer it: Proceed to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honours. If we could scroll down or have the whole page on the screen, it would appreciate me [sic]. There it is, J.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, at J, the Prosecution in their telephonic discussion with you recorded you as saying: He is aware of a Saha Kurspahic, an old lady he believes she was left behind by the group on the day of fire and was picked up by the bus, and was, therefore, not killed in the fire. And the question that I have for you, sir, do you agree with me now that Saha Kurspahic listed as victim number 53 approximately 70 years old in 1992 on the Prosecution's list is incorrect and should be taken off the list?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Cole. Just a minute. Witness, Witness. Please listen to me. Counsel is on his feet. When counsel is on his feet, you stop. What do you have to say, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, the question is assuming evidence -- matters that are not in evidence putting together the name and a person on the schedule in the indictment. Now, that is an improper way to deal with the witness. If I can just have a moment, yes, counsel in his question is assuming that the information on the exhibit before the witness is necessarily tied into the name on the annex, and I think it's unfair to the witness to frame the question in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree. Don't put the questions in that way, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How else am I going to do that, Your Honour, we are going to be here all day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just ask him whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If there's another Saha Kurspahic perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, or whether he has knowledge as to whether that person was alive or dead on the relevant date. But I think Mr. Cole does have a point. It's not for the witness to say whether a name should or should not be on the list. We will decide that ultimately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to Saha Kurspahic, is there anyone else by that name or is there just the one person that we've been talking about that would have been in Visegrad in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: There was no other. She was not burnt in the fire. It's an old woman who was left behind the column. I stated at the last hearing that she survived the fire, but I attended her funeral later on. There were no two Saha's. Maybe it's just the same person twice. She was not killed in the fire. She survived it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is this common knowledge that you believe ought to be known to VG-18, VG-78, VG-84, and VG-13 and were they at the funeral?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. With us Bosniaks, Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. He has answered the question. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we look at your item K and it says: "He is aware of" -- we shouldn't go down further. We shouldn't go down further because that's the part that should be redacted. It says: "He is aware of a Hajraga [phoen] Sehic, who was not filled in the fire." And the question I have to is ask you is this: In Annex A of the indictment, we have -- we have at item number 66 a Haraga Sehic, have you ever heard of a Haraga Sehic existing in Koritnik in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I knew Hajro Sehic, a man who lived in Mala Gostilje, which is close to Koritnik; however, I was not at Koritnik at the time. I cannot tell you anything about it. He was an elderly person. I don't know if he is still alive or not. I do know, however, that my father told me this man was not at Pionirska Street when the fire took place. I don't know what happened with that person, and he was not an inhabitant of my village in Koritnik where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask that we now go into private session to discuss the remainder of his clarifications to protect the identity of other individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Mr. Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you just confirm, please, sir that you and I haven't spoken today before your testimony?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No, we haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And can I say at the outset that I'm sorry that you've had to come here again and at such short notice too. I just want to go through some preliminary matters to put your testimony into perspective, and if you would, if you could try just to keep your answers as short as you can for me unless there is a necessary explanation as part of your answer. You were a policeman in Visegrad in 1992, early 1992.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: You left Visegrad in April 1992 to go to Medjedja?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, well, September 1991, the 21st of September, mobilisation of the reserve police station, reserve force of the police station and I went home two or three times to have a bath and so on, but otherwise I was in Medjedja, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, your address in Visegrad, did you live in Pionirska Street?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Pionirska number 11, Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How far is that house from the house where your relatives and friends were burned to death in June?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: About a 100 to 110 metres. Not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, when you finally abandoned your house in 1992, are you aware of who moved into the house?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Milan Lukic and his Lukics were in my house, and they kept a goat on the upper story.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, I'm sorry, sir, to reminds you again, but can you confirm, please, for us, that you lost some close members of your family in the Pionirska fire, your mother, Hata; your sister, Hasiba, known as Hana; your sister, Kada Sehic; and your nephew, Faruk Sehic, son of Kada; can you confirm that is correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you also lost many other relatives and acquaintances in that fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: All of them are relatives, except this man, Redzo Memisevic, all the others were relations of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And your father Hasib was one of the few persons who escaped from the burning house?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And he was interviewed shortly after his escape from that house on video, and you can confirm that video interview is an exhibit in this trial?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's the first time he gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour that I've been advised that we are in private session and there's no need to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kurspahic --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: We were talking about your father who escaped from the burning Pionirska house in 1992. Your father subsequently passed away in 1996?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, you testified for the first time in the Mitar Vasiljevic trial in 2001?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And during that trial, the list of 51 names produced as Exhibit P39 was produced during that trial, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And I ask that that be shown to you now, both the English and the B/C/S versions. Yes. Does the Court have the B/C/S version? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: It's in two pages, I think.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I can see it, but it's very small print.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: On the right-hand side we have the English, can you see on the left-hand side the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. So you recall that was produced at the first trial in 2001?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you didn't compile that list yourself. That was compiled by somebody else, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I did not compile it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you were called to testify again in this trial and you testified on the 1st of September last year?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And at the first trial and just prior to testifying in September last year, you advised the Court on the first occasion, and the Prosecution on the second occasion, that you believed that the names of Jasarevic should have been Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, it is then that I said it. There was a mistake made by someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Right. As early as the first trial in 2001, you believed that the name Jasarevic should have been Halilovic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, and I asked for that to be corrected. I wasn't the one making the corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, perhaps we can just deal with P39 which is in front of you at the moment. I just want to ask you about some of the names in it. And this list as we see it was subsequently corrected on a couple of occasions by you, as you've just indicated, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So try and do it in an orderly fashion, we won't go through all the names but this is the list that was prepared by somebody else and featured in the Mitar Vasiljevic trial in 2001. The first name, number 1, Medo Kurspahic, aged about 50 years; do you believe that that person at item number 1 perished in the Pionirska fire or not?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: He was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I am sorry, in English that doesn't completely answer the question. Did he perish in the Pionirska fire in your belief?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: 100 percent. He, his wife, Mustafa and their daughter, Medina.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If we move down to item number 9 -- sorry, number 10. It reads Kurspahic a surname only, daughter of Mujesira aged 10 year?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Mujesira.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mujesira. Are you able to give us the name of the girl aged about 10 years. The first name of number 10?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, I can. If you allow me a moment. In that family of Mujesira there were two children. The wife was Mujesira, daughter Anesa and daughter Halida, one born in 1979, the other one in 1982, and their grandmother Sumbula.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If we can just try and concentrate on the question, please, Mr. Kurspahic. Are you able to give us the name of the first name of the 10-year-old daughter of Mujesira who perished in the fire in Pionirska?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: One was Anesa the other one was Halida. One was born in 1979, the other one in 1982. They were two girls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could know what was before him -- there's a folded piece of paper, if we could have a copy of that and know what that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, what are you looking at? Witness, just tell us, don't listen to Mr. Ivetic right now. Just tell us, what is it you are looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is no document of sorts. This is a list with first and last names and years of birth per family. People are listed per family and per household and those are the same people that are on your list. I can leave this with you if you wish, Mr. President, for your perusal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you prepare that list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where does it come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the census, and we went by the last names and households. They are disputing that Aisa appeared at the health clinic, where she was burnt; and then for Medo who supposedly launched an application, whereas he was killed. So you have people there by family name. I can give it to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you want it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, can I indicate I haven't seen the list. I'm unaware of what is in it, I would suggest it's appropriate if it's a list compiled by this witness that it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to see it first before it's admitted, Your Honours. I might have submissions on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let it be passed to counsel and then to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's nothing to hide here. Give it to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: First to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if it is submitted by the Prosecution for admission at this late stage I believe the Prosecution's case had rested and this is rejoinder evidence; or I don't know what it is, actually, what stage we are in, but causes some technical problem, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a list by families stating who came from which family or household.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, to the extent the list has no names that were not even on the original annex of victim, so to the extent the Prosecution so seeking to amend their charges at this late stage [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Prosecution is not seeking to do anything. Just show them the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not correct. No one was added to the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, the last page says in Serbian, the word is [B/C/S/spoken], which in English -- let me see how it's coming up, I don't see how it was translated which to me indicates that this is a list prepared by someone else giving suggestions and reminders to the witnesses as to how he should testify. I think we need him to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please pass the list to counsel and let us get on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can keep it. I don't need it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I've had the opportunity, Your Honour, to have a look at it. It's obviously a list and the writing --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can tell what you it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Don't speak until you are asked to answer a question. Let's hear from Mr. Cole first.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Of course I understand what it says in addition to the list of names, but I can lay some foundation, find out a bit more about it from the witness and ask for it to be admitted at that stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Witness, the list in front of you, who was the person that physically compiled that list and put it together?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: We organised this in terms of families. For example, I couldn't remember the name of a child who was three years old, and now when the Prosecutor asked me what the name of the child was, that's why I did this. For no other reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What I would like to find out from you, just briefly, is how many people firstly collaborated in gathering that information that is in the list before you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: We did, from the different families and households. Every person stated their father's, mother's last name, people did this by families. No institution or organisation was involved. We gave up on this Tribunal or anything else. We were unable to get by any information of the deceased and loved ones for a number of years now. We gave up on seeking justice.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can we do it this way, the list is material that's been gathered from all the interested parties, those that have lost family members in the fire, the information has been gathered together, and a list of that material has been put together. Does that sum it up?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. That was the next thing I was going to ask you. You are referring to that list now, do you believe that list to be correct and authentic in the information that is contained therein?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: 99 percent.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. So 99 percent, are you able to point to anything in it that isn't correct or can you just tell us why you say 99 rather than 100?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Well, I can tell you that it's 2.000 percent accurate, but I'm trying to say that it is authentic, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, on that basis he has testified here I would ask that the list of names be entered into evidence and be given an exhibit number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did he also participate in gathering this information?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Witness, did you contribute to the information that is contained in the list yourself?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes, my mother disappeared as well as two of my cousins, uncles, friends, neighbours. We all got together from each of the households, if any family member survived, then they provided me with years of birth and names. I could not have known each and every child if I didn't live with that child.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it should be marked for identification since we don't have a copy in the official language of the Tribunal in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it in B/C/S in its entirely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's in B/C/S, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, then, yes, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I was going to suggest, Your Honour, that it can be admitted now. The witness can sign it with today's date and time. There can be copies made thereafter. It can immediately then become an exhibit. Probably no reason to be marked for identification can be taken from him at the conclusion of his testimony and copied, translated at that time, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the practice I've followed in the last ten years of this Tribunal unless it's an official language it's marked for identification until translation is provided and can be verified, and the document can be -- know of -- right now the lead counsel for the Defence doesn't even know this document and cannot read it so I don't know what kind of submissions we can make on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll maintain the ruling that it's marked for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P333, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Witness, we were going through, I think, the list of in front of you on the screen, P39, dealing with some of the names on the list, and we are not going to do all of them. And I think you had given us the name of two daughters of Mujesira who perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm now going to move down to item 14, the name at number 14, the Ismeta. It shows Ismeta Kurspahic, daughter-in-law of Osman and Ajka about 26 years old. Is that a correct reference of a person who perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you were asked about this earlier, do you know --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Besides the lady who died in the fire, do you know any other Ismeta Kurspahics that are alive or were alive after the date of the fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: There is one, a cousin of mine in Bihac. She is a permanent resident there. She only comes to visit once or twice a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you know of no others?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: There are no others in the village of Koritnik, in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Right. Now, let's just make clear once and for all the situation in relation to Aisa Kurspahic. If you'll have a look at the list, you'll see there are two Aisa Kurspahics, one at number 22 and one at number 24. You see those? Yes, you've got too many documents in front of you. It was a list of 51 names that were used during the --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: 24, Aisa, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: 22, Aisa. Now, you subsequently made a correction to this list --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: The one under 22, that one survived. The Aisa under 24 was killed. The one under 22 is the person who survived who at the time was about 22 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you. So the lady listed at number 24 perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, please have a look -- I'm trying to do this as expeditiously as we can, have a look at number 23, Ramiza Kurspahic, and then have a look at number 41, the same name.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Ramiza under 23, she did not take part in the incident. She survived. The other one is Becar Kurspahic's wife, and she perished in Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So the lady at number 41 perished in the fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you corrected the references to the two other ladies at 22 and 23, you corrected that and indicated that they should not have been on the list previously, didn't you?
