utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, let's go through to number 37 [sic] on the list, Hasiba Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: It is my father. He was involved and survived. After the blast, a door opened and he fell out. He survived. This is my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. And that he was incorrectly listed in this list in the Vasiljevic trial, and you subsequently corrected that entry to show that he should no longer have been amongst the list of the dead, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, if we go down to number 39, Hana Kurspahic, about 30 years old, daughter of Hata and Hasib, does that appear to you to be reference to your sister Hasiba, whose real name is Hasiba, who actually perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Because you told us before that she was sometimes known as Hana, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Most of the people in the village knew her as Hana; however in the register, her name is listed as Hasiba.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. Moving on, at number 44, we see Kada Sehic, about 39 years old. Do you believe that that refers to your sister, maiden name Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: She perished in the Pionirska fire, didn't she?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, she did as well as her son Faruk.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And Faruk is listed under her name at number 45?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And we'll just for completeness, numbers 48, 49 and 50, people with the name Jasarevic, you've been asked a number of times about these people -- just a moment, please, Mr. Kurspahic. Can we just -- can you go through them -- let's deal with 48 first. Do you say that Mujo Jasarevic perished in the fire, or should it be Mujo Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, Mujo perished in the fire. As well as Meho and Meho's wife, Tima, their last name was Halilovic. I told the Defence there was two Mujos. There was a Halilovic and Jasarevic, Mujo; one perished, the little or small Mujo. There was a separate hamlet of Halilovici there.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Now, number 50 is Hajra, are you saying it was Hajra Halilovic who perished in the fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, Meho's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, have you heard the name Mujo Jasarevic before?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I knew the man. I knew both Mujo's, Jasarevic and Halilovic, I knew both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Is the surname Jasarevic a very common name?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: In one parts of the Sase village, you have the Jasarevics and in the other part of the hamlet, you have the Halilovics. They are both the Jasarevic and the Halilovic families there.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm asking you is Jasarevic a very common name for a person to have?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: For example, do you know how many Mujo Jasarevics do you know?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I know one person by the last name of Jasarevic, and another under the name of Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Is it your belief that nobody by the name of Jasarevic perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No, those were the Halilovics. Meho and Mujo were next door neighbours. I know that Meho's last name was Halilovic, as well as that of his wife, Hajra. And as I've said, I wasn't sure whether Mujo Halilovic or Jasarevic was killed. His wife's name was Mujesira and you can check that if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. I want you just to put aside the three Jasarevics we've just been talking about there. Wasn't there, in fact, one other Jasarevic who in fact did perish in the Pionirska fire in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No, all of these were Halilovics: Meho, and Tima. Their last name certainly is Halilovic. I am not sure of Mujo, whether he was a Halilovic or a Jasarevic. I don't know whether any other Jasarevics were involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Well, what about Tima Jasarevic, is that person one of the victims of the fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: This needs to be revised. Their last name is Halilovic. It should be done here before the Bench. Halilovic, I told that to the Defence as well. Meho and Hajra Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just see if we can deal with that now. How many people then by the name of Halilovic do you say -- just a moment. How many people by the surname of Halilovic do you say perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Meho and Hajra, their last name was Halilovic. I'm not certain about Mujo, he was either a Jasarevic or a Halilovic, and he perished.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Well, what I'll do now is just go through some of the names in the Annex A, which is the list of names attached to the indictment. I'm not sure, have you been given that list of names?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I only have the old original version with 70 plus names, and then there's the list of 51 names, I have that one as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What was the list that was given to you by counsel earlier, I just want to be clear what that is that you have? Could I have a look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. I have never seen that before, as I said at the outset. I've never seen this list before.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, the document that I've just had a look at that you were given before, you say you've never seen it before, I'm not sure if it was explained to you precisely what it was, but that is a copy of the indictment in this trial alleging serious crimes against Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic. And at the back of that indictment, it has two annexes: Annex A which is a list of those killed in the burning house at Pionirska Street, there are 70 names there; and Annex B, a list of 16 known persons that were among those killed in the burning house at Bikavac nearly two weeks later. So that was the document you were looking at before. I see counsel has taken it back now, but I'm going to go through just some of the names of those that are noted in Annex A to the indictment as being killed in that burning house in Pionirska. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could I just ask Your Honours, are we taking a break at 1:15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, we are going to go to 1.45. It's a mini-marathon.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Mr. Kurspahic, the first one I'm going to ask you about is number 4, you don't have the list in front of you before, but number 4 says Jasmina Delija, approximately 24 years old. And the age -- just a moment. Wait a moment -- the age that I'm going to give you now is the age at the time that these -- it is said these persons were killed in Pionirska Street. So that's back in 1992. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. With Jasmina Delija, approximately 24 years old in 1992, do you believe that a person by that name was burned to death in the Pionirska house?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, she burnt to death, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And what was her maiden name?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Kurspahic. She is a relative of mine. Close relative.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Now, listed in the Annex A four Jasarevics, I think in terms of completeness I've got to put this to you once again. We have listed as, perhaps I can just do it by way of leading. We have at number 6, Tima Jasarevic, age unknown - and if you can do it in a yes or no fashion - do you believe that a person by the name of Tima Jasarevic perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Tima Jasarevic, it's Tima Velic and her mother, they were mentioned as having been in that house at the critical time, their surname is Velic, Ima and Nurka, mother and daughter. And at that critical time, they were in the vicinity of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I am he not going to ask you about those persons, but is Tima Jasarevic a person who you say should, in fact, be Tima Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, Halilovic. I've already said that, that it's Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the next one we have is Hajra, H-a-j-r-a, Jasarevic, approximately 35 years old, do you believe that person should be Hajra Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Hajra Halilovic, Meho Halilovic's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So that is you are saying yes, that should be Hajra?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. Number 8 is Meho Jasarevic, approximately 42 years old. Do you say that name should be Meho Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the next one Mujo Jasarevic, approximately 47 years old, do you say that person should be, in fact, Mujo Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. The Aisa Kurspahic at number 10, A-i-s-a, approximately 49 years old, that person you've told us previously was burned to death at Pionirska?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If we go down, you don't have the list, but it's number 15, listen to this carefully, the first name is Aner, A-n-e-r, Kurspahic, approximately 6 years old. Just hold it for a moment, please. So that person is listed there. Do you believe that a person called Aner Kurspahic, approximately 6 years old, was burned to death in the Pionirska fire or not?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Aida is the right name. Her real name is Aida. A-i-d-a.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I think something might have gone wrong with it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you are asking about the 6-year-old boy, Aner.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And I spelled it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He is asking about the 6-year-old boy Aner not Aida, not the lady whose name is Aida. You can help --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can help, Your Honours, I believe the witness is talking about number 11 because the question before Mr. Cole was number 10 on the list, so I think the witness is referring to number 11 on the list which is the name he mentioned so --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, witness, we'll just clarify this, I've moved down to number 15, just a moment, I've moved down to number 15 we are not going to go through all of the names, and I'm asking you about Aner, A-n-e-r, Kurspahic at number 15 who it says is approximately six years old.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: It says here on my list under number 15, Aida Kurspahic, maybe that's a mistake in the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, witness, you have before you the previous exhibit, I think probably the best idea is for that to be removed from the screen now. I'll just repeat it. What I'm asking you about now is a list that you don't have in front of you which is an annex to the indictment that contains a list of 70 names. It was the list that counsel had provided to you before but which he has now taken back, so you don't have it before you. So I'm just going to give the number on the list, what the name is, and the age and ask you about the person. So I'm asking you now about number 15 Aner Kurspahic, approximately six years old. Do you believe that that person -- a person of that name and that approximate age was burned to death in the Pionirska fire in 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. It's Hidajet's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: About what age was the Aner Kurspahic, do you believe, the one that perished in the fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Five or six, I'm not quite sure. It says Almir, and there were three children and they all perished together, the brother, sister, and this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd ask Mr. Cole where is that contained in the clarification and the proofing session that was provided to us or otherwise notice to the Defence. This is new evidence. I've never heard it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I don't know what counsel was saying it was so fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me slow down then. I'd ask Mr. Cole where is this contained in the proofing statement, the clarifications by this witness that were provided by the Prosecution after Mr. Cole's telephone discussion with him as notice for this new evidence that is being led.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object to new evidence being led at this late stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm conducting a cross-examination here. I'm not here to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's a Chamber witness, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, Mr. Cole gave us a clarification identifying Aner Kurspahic and giving us totally different information. Now we are finding out for the first time that he intends to prove it's different person. If the Prosecution is going to reply upon it in their case, Your Honour, it's new evidence, needs to be noticed. I have a right to challenge it and confront it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, you'll recall that the witness indicated he hasn't been spoken to anyone since that phone call in March. We might find out when I ask him in a moment where this information has come from and why it's new. But now he is here, now he is a court witness. We are entitled to hear anything he has to say about anyone who is victim or alleged to be a victim. I'd like to find out more about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kurspahic, you've heard the exchange here, you've just given some evidence about an Aner Kurspahic, approximately six years old. Have you ever -- I think you've given the name of the -- have you given the name of the parent? What was the name of the parent of this Aner Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Hidajet. There's Aner Kurspahic, Omer's son, he did not perish. He is in Austria. He was taken away. He and his father and his uncle took them out of a car and were disposed of by Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So you are telling the Court now about this Aner Kurspahic whose son of Halida who perished in the Pionirska fire. Do you recall having mentioned that to anyone on a previous occasion, or its the first time that you are telling that information to the Court?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Well, I talked about this on the basis of the list. I revised the list for all the people who hadn't perished, and we did that earlier on. We crossed out the names of people who were not there. Now, what the critical people are, well, I'd like to help you to clarify whether they did perish or didn't. So tell me who you mean specifically, who you want to know about specifically?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Witness, we just need to clarify this situation with Aner Kurspahic and how many of them there are and who their parents are. Yes. So Mr. Kurspahic, can we just concentrate on Aner Kurspahic, the one who is in the indictment at number 15, the boy about six, and the mother is Halida, are you able to give us any further details about this Aner Kurspahic before I ask you about another one?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: There was Hidajet. Omer's boy was ten or 12 and this other one was five or six years old, and that was Hidajet's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Aner Kurspahic, daughter of Halida, what was the father's name, the father of the boy who died in the fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Hidajet.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Hidajet was the father, was it Halida the mother?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Ismeta, the mother's name was Ismeta. She is Hidajet's wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is not contained in the Ewa Tabeau's list of possible persons, so this is completely new evidence that is now being led out of thin air.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, can you clarify for me is the examination to the effect that there are two persons with the name Aner Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I was just going to ask him about the other one because it's certainly -- it's in the disclosed material from the phone call on the 4th of March. I was trying to separate them and get his explanation for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kurspahic, I'm just going to draw your attention to a document which was produced as a result of the telephone call that you had on the 4th of March, and I'm going to read out what this document records was said between you and counsel on that occasion, if you just listen carefully, please. This document says that during the phone call you said that you believed that a person called Aner Kurspahic, son of Latifa Kurspahic, is alive and in Austria. Now, just hold it for a moment. First I'm going to ask you, did you say that during the telephone call on the 1st of March, or do you recall saying that? That's the first thing, there are other questions to come.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't remember. Possibly but I don't remember saying that. I know for sure that Aner is Latifa's son and that he was killed with his father and uncle Fikret. I'm here to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So you are aware of Aner Kurspahic who is the son of a Latifa Kurspahic, and your evidence today is that that that Aner Kurspahic is no longer alive?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And when do you believe that he lost his life?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Before what happened in Pionirska Street, they set off for Belgrade. His mother, Latifa; his father, Hasan; his grandfather, Omer; and uncle, Fikret, who was a military person. He came to take them to Belgrade and from a private vehicle, Milan Lukic pursuant to Latifa's statement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness kindly be asked to slow down and tell us the story one by one, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, you were speak too fast. You are going too fast. Now, I am going to ask you to repeat it, but Mr. Ivetic has something to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This individual is now testifying about something unrelated but which is interesting to me because to my knowledge I see no statements of Latifa Kurspahic anywhere, so I don't know where this witness's knowledge of Latifa Kurspahic comes from, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, he can tell us. Witness, would you repeat more slowly what you just said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness be asked to make pauses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I talked to his grandfather, Hasan, who survived and then died later, so Hasan's son, Fikret, came by from Belgrade and he was an army officer. He came to take his father, his mother, his brother, the family away; and when they left Visegrad, in a passenger vehicle, privately owned, driven by Omer, there was his son there, Aner, who was ten or 12 years old, and his brother; and in the bus there was Hasan, Meva, their daughter-in-law, Latifa, and her small daughter, and then Milan took Hasan out. He took all three of them out of the car and another person from the bus, and I don't know what the name of that person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I note the time, could I just finish up on this subject. It will only take a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm just going to give you an opportunity to tell the Court or give an explanation or whether you remember, you actually said this comment during the telephone conversation with counsel on the 4th of March. This is what is written and this is what was supplied to the Defence, that you believed that Aner Kurspahic -- this is what is written here, that you believed that Aner Kurspahic, son of Latifa Kurspahic, is alive and in Austria. Now, just hold it there a moment. I'm going to ask you a question. Do you believe that you said that, or that it's a mistake, or how would you explain that that comment has been written down following the conversation that you had with counsel?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I'm not sure that that is what I said. I really don't remember. And if even if I did say that, then I withdraw it. I don't remember ever having said that. I don't know, I'm not sure. Now, I couldn't say what actually did not happen, that's not something I do, but I'm here to explain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, is that an appropriate time or are we going through 1.45, I've got it wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry, you did indicate that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to move on now to in this list of 70 names that has been attached to the indictment, I think you've been given that back now, have a look at number 25 on the list, that shows Hana Kurspahic, approximately 30 years old. It's probably in English, but it says 25, Hana Kurspahic, approximately 30 years old. That's what is written here. You can see the name Hana, can you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that's my sister. But there are two names. She also comes under number 27, and Hasiba is her real name, so you should delete the other number.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Just a moment. There is a Hana Kurspahic approximately 30 years old. How many Hana Kurspahics do you know?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Her nickname is Hana, but her real name is Hasiba. It's the same person under number 25 and 27. 25 and 27 are the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, I'm just going to suggest to you, Mr. Kurspahic, that they are two separate people. That a Hana, just a moment, that a Hana Kurspahic and also a Hasiba Kurspahic both perished in the Pionirska fire, one of them being your sister, and one of them being another woman. Just would you think about that for a moment and tell us whether you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No, no, that's not true. The truth is that it's one and the same person. There was just one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So just to be clear then, your sister's name was Hasiba. She perished in the fire; correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And on the list that you've produced and that you've brought with you and which will now be an exhibit, is there also a separate person -- separate victim with the first name of Hana Kurspahic in addition to Hasiba?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No, no. Listen to me. There might be a mistake. I don't know about my list, but the list I have in front of me were 70 names, that's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: His evidence is that Hana Kurspahic at number 25 and Hasiba Kurspahic at 27 are one and the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: He has made that clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. And his sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, he believes that Hasiba Kurspahic and Hana, it's the same person, his sister goes under the name of Hana.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer do you have, Mr. Cole?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: In fairness, I'm not sure, Your Honour; but I don't know -- I'm certainly not going through all the names, maybe half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The next name I'm going to ask you about is number 28, and that reads Hasnija, H-a-s-n-i-j-a, Kurspahic approximately 62 years old.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: This is a mistake. Hasnija, no, there's Pasija, so it's the same person. Pasija has a daughter and her name is Hasnija, but she didn't perish in the fire. She wasn't there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Let's just do it precisely if we can. Concentrating on Hasnija approximately 62 years old, was there a person of that name who perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And are you saying that name doesn't appear on the list that you brought with you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No, it's not on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that Hasnija, that I have just referred to at number 28, is the same person as the Pasana or Pasija in item 50?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, they are mother and daughter. They are two different people, mother and daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Who were mother and daughter?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Pasija is Hasnija's mother, and Hasnija wasn't there in Pionirska Street in Visegrad when the house was set on fire, but Pasija was.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you say Pasana Kurspahic was the mother of Hasnija Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, if you see the age for Pasana Kurspahic, that's age 56, and the age of Hasnija Kurspahic is approximately 62 years old?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No, Hasnija might be about 30 roughly. This is not correct here. Somebody wrote that but it's not correct. I don't know. Hasnija might have been 30, whereas Pasnija is her mother, about 60. 58, 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Was this 30-year-old Hasnija killed in the fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was her mother killed in the fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And she was about 60, you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 58, 60. An elderly woman. She has children older than Hasnija too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And her name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pasija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, this is -- and Mr. Groome, this is getting a little confusing. What I'm going to do is at the end of the examination, I'm going to ask each party to make submissions as to the names that should be taken off the list as a result of the evidence that we have heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it occurs to me that, and I apologise that there is this confusion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Don't give any evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No. I would like an opportunity to just -- after Mr. Kurspahic finishes his testimony to sit down with him and go through this list, who put it together. It seems to be, from what I can gather here, if it was done with the different family members --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He is giving evidence. He in the middle -- 17

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, I am saying when he has concluded his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, when he has concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before he returns, I'm going to ask for an opportunity just to sit down with him and go through this other list that it seems has been compiled with the assistance of all the family members who really are the people in the best position. We have tried to provide the Chamber with data sources and recollections of different people. It seems that Mr. Kurspahic has invested quite a bit of time and gathered the help that he needed to come up with a rather reliable list, so I am going to ask to be able to explore that with him later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm having another idea, it's something equivalent to yours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, what are you going to do with the information that you will gather when you have spoken with the witness after he has completed his evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I was actually going to ask Mr. Cole to sit down with an investigator and really get down to the bottom of this once and for all. I would ask that we do that tonight, disclose it to Mr. Ivetic, and if Mr. Ivetic wants to be present, I would have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And then if necessary, to have Mr. Kurspahic -- if it was necessary for him to spend a few minutes just describing any of the source of the material, that he could do that tomorrow morning and perhaps this list that he has worked on would be considered the authoritative list. I think, Your Honours, it would still also be important, though, to verify it against what we do know from data sources, so I think prudence would require just to check it against what information we know from the census and the other data sources. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 17 years ago. Microphone. Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour, it should have been done.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why don't we just do it in court and take the witness through the list one by one?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no objection to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Because he apparently has the information. We have 70 names and we could ask him to comment on each name. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's, I believe, what we did with CW1 to a certain extent so I can't object to it being done. We will make submissions based upon that because there are certain other elements as to reliability, credibility, et cetera, but I have no problem doing that if its' --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see Mr. Sredoje Lukic has had a toilet break, so we are going to adjourn now and we'll resume at 2.15. Please consider the proposal that I've made, Mr. Cole and Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the break, the Chamber considered the matter, and in the result we'll just have Mr. Cole conclude his examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. What I would indicate is that I think there's been a problem, a little bit of confusion, so I would like to go through each name in the Annex A with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're going to do the task that I said I would undertake. All right. Well, let's proceed very quickly, then, if that's what you're going to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could just briefly, for the record, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, and of course Your Honours, can put to the witness anything they want in terms of the manner of questioning. However, we would want to reaffirm the statements that Mr. Alarid made during the testimony or after the testimony of CW1 as to what effect that is, and that we cannot just merely treat this as a manner of curing the Prosecution's case and whether they've met the burden of proof at this late stage of the game by simply taking persons incorrectly on the list, taking them off. The effect of that is much more widespread and goes toward the credibility and the truthfulness of the entire Prosecution case on this count and the witnesses that have come during the Prosecution case to testify, and I would just, again, reiterate that all the statements that Mr. Alarid made, I can read through them but I don't think it's necessary, they're in the transcript during CW1, continue to apply and continue to be the Defence's position and objection to merely curing the Prosecution's indictment at this stage, given the testimony that has been there because obviously I would reopen Pandora's box and the case would have to be recalled and it would violate that double jeopardy and we would put to witnesses of the Prosecution different questions if we had a different list to work with. The indictment is the instrument by which the accused is put on notice --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel, slow down, please, for the interpreters. Please slow down. MR. IVETIC. ... Respond to that indictment. This is not the time and place to be making any new indictments with any new witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. We note the submissions that you have made. Yes, Mr. Cole. Now let us move quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Mr. Kurspahic, you have brought along today a list which contains a list of those persons whom you believe were killed in the Pionirska fire in Visegrad in 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: That list is the result of input from yourself and relatives of the deceased victims; correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could I just ask you briefly what resources you consulted other than relatives in compiling the list. I just want to go through, if you could say yes or no to these resources. Did you consult the International Committee of the Red Cross, their resources?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: They have everything about these missing people. They are on record as missing, but nothing has been lately done. We in the family compiled the list because of those children whose ages we were not certain about.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Mr. Kurspahic, could you just please concentrate on the question so we can move through this promptly. I want to ask you about some resources, whether you consulted them in arriving at your list. Did you consult the resources of the International Committee of the Red Cross, their resources; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: This is not a criticism, sir. Did you consult any of the censuses from 1991 or onwards? Once again, it's not a criticism. Did you consult any census records in compiling the list?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: The 1991 census. I have that census, which is authentic, reliable, and you can get that census too. It's available to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you consult voters' records?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I have the complete material from the municipality of Visegrad, all the lists of the population and the census.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you consult the voters' records?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you consult the resources of the International Committee For Missing Persons?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Now, how many people in total, Mr. Kurspahic, do you believe lost their lives in the Pionirska fire in June 1992? The total number is what?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: There's nothing to think about; exactly 53 people were killed in the -- in the torching of that house. I made the complete list.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So what's the total number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He said 53.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Does the list you brought with you have 53 names or some other number?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: 53. There's no other number. It's the one and only list.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm going to go through the names in the indictment Annex A very briefly and quickly, and if you need to consult your list, please do so. And if you could just tell us whether you believe each person as I read the name to you perished in the Pionirska fire or not. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Before answering, please feel free to check the list that you brought with you. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 1 -- and do you have a copy of the list before you where it says "Annex A" and then 70 names?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: That's the list I'm going to go through. You consult your list if you need to. Number 1: Mula Ajanovic, approximately 75 years old. Did she perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 2, Adis Delija, approximately 2 years old. Did that child perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 3, Ajnija Delija, approximately 53 years old. And please forgive me if I'm not aware if it's masculine or feminine. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, it's a female, Ajnija.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And if the name needs to be corrected, the spelling needs to be corrected, can you indicate that please. The next one, you've testified previously, number 4, Jasmina Delija, approximately 24 years old. That person -- that woman did perish in the Pionirska fire.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 5, it doesn't give a family name, just a first name: Hasena, age unknown. Are you able to say whether someone of that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I can't say anything for certain. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The next one is Tima Jasarevic, age unknown, number 6. Do you believe that person perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Her last name is not Jasarevic. I told you before. You have the new list. Let's work with that list, please. I have that list, and the Defence has it too.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. So what you say for number 6, the person who perished was Tima Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So we'll change Jasarevic to Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Sorry. Tima Jasarevic was Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, he actually testified it was Tima Velic earlier, as well, so I don't know what we'd put on it. We need clarification of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm going to go through each --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's Velic, Velic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it Tima Velic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tima Velic, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which, for the record, Your Honours, is number 69 on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. We'll deal with it that way. What -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: We're going to go through in chronological order. We're at number 6, and just to clarify that, was there a person called Tima Jasarevic who perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And was there a person called Tima Halilovic who perished in the Pionirska fire? If you don't know, please say so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He's checking his notes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 7, Hajra Jasarevic, approximately 35 years old. Did a person by that name perish in the Pionirska fire, or was it another surname, Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: The last name is Halilovic, and she was killed; right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The next one is Meho Jasarevic, approximately 42 years old. Did a person by that name perish in the Pionirska fire, or was the surname, in fact, Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Halilovic is the last name; right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the next one, number 9. In relation to Meho Halilovic, did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Next one, number 9, Mujo Jasarevic, approximately 47 years old. Is that, in fact, Mujo Halilovic who perished in the --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Halilovic. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. So Mujo Halilovic, approximately 47, perished in the Pionirska fire. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 10, Aisa Kurspahic, approximately 47 years old. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 11, Aida Kurspahic, approximately 12 years old. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 12, Ajka, A-j-k-a, Kurspahic, approximately 62 years old. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 13, Alija Kurspahic, approximately 55 years old. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 14, Almir, A-l-m-i-r, Kurspahic, approximately 10 years old. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you've told us previously Aner Kurspahic, approximately 6 years old, did perish in the Pionirska fire. Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: It could be a mistake here. It could be Vahid instead of Almir. We need to correct that. The right first name is Vahid, son of Idajit [phoen], not Almir.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So was it Aner? Do you believe there was an Aner Kurspahic who perished in the Pionirska fire or not?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 16, Becar, B-e-c-a-r, Kurspahic, approximately 52 years old. Do you believe that person perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 17, Bisera Kurspahic, approximately 50 years old. Do you know --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I have to ask the question. Do you believe that person perished in the Pionirska fire. Your answer's yes?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Bula Kurspahic, did that person -- aged approximately 58 years. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 19, Dzheva, D-z-h-e-v-a, Kurspahic, approximately 22 years old. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 20, Enesa Kurspahic, approximately 2 years old, E-n-e-s-a. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fie?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 21, surname Kurspahic, first name unknown, approximately 2 days old. Do you know the name of that person, that baby?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No. It's an infant who hadn't even got a name.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And was there such an infant without a name that perished in the Pionirska fire age about 2 days old?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. It was exactly 2 days old. The woman gave birth two days prior to the fire in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What was the name of the mother of that baby? Was it Sadeta, S-a-d-e --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, Sadeta, daughter of Muhamed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. Number 22, Hasa, H-a-s-a, Kurspahic, approximately 18 years old. Do you believe that person perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 23, Hajrija Kurspahic, H-a-j-r-i-j-a, Kurspahic, approximately 60 years old. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 24, Halida Kurspahic, H-a-l-i-d-a, approximately 10 years old. Did that person perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, I think he explained already, but I just want to have it in the evidence at this stage. Number 6, 7, 8, and 9, Jasarevic, which he says is Halilovic, what was the explanation, Witness, as to why that was a mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I did not write this list with Jasarevic in it. The right, correct family name is Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, I'm just going to ask you about items 25 and 27, and you testified about these items before: 25, Hana Kurspahic, approximately 30 years old; and Hasiba Kurspahic, number 27, age unknown. Was it your testimony before that those two entries are in relation to the same person, your sister?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, your sister, how old was she at the time of the fire in 1992? What was her age then?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Born 1952, the 13th of May, 1952, so her age was exactly 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And was it your testimony before that you are unaware of any other person by the name of Hana Kurspahic or Hasiba Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you just give us your sister Hasiba's date of birth again.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. I think it's the 13th, but I'm no longer sure of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What year? Was she your older or younger sister?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I was born in 1950; she was born in 1952.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So that means if she was born in 1952, that in 1992 she was 40. Wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: A slip of the tongue. She was 40, right. 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. So you'll see that the entries we've got here, one is aged approximately 30, the other age unknown; but your sister, you confirm, was age 40 in 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to ask you about -- and your sister perished in the Pionirska fire, didn't she?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 26, Hasan Kurspahic, H-a-s-a-n, approximately 50 years old, and I'll remind you that these are the ages in 1992. Did a person by that name, do you believe, perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 28, Hasnija, H-a-s-n-i-j-a, Kurspahic, approximately 62 years old. Did a person by that name perish, in your belief, in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No. Her mother is Pasnija, and she is not Hasnija. She was not Hasnija. She was around 35, and she wasn't killed. She did not perish.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Do you know a Hasnija Kurspahic, approximately 62 years old in 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. I know the younger woman Hasnija who was the daughter of Pasnija, 30ish or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So have you ever met a Hasnija Kurspahic who was 62 in 1992 or heard anything about a person of that age?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: It's a mistake. It's Pasija, 62 years old, Pasija, the mother of this Hasnija woman. I said that previously for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: No, I just need to finally deal with this name here, so do you -- do you know now or have you ever known a Hasnija Kurspahic who was 62 years of age in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in this exchange alone, Your Honours. The witness has been very adamant, very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr ...

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm finished there. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Mr. Kurspahic, number 29, Hata, H-a-t-a, Kurspahic, approximately 68 years old. Do you believe a person by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, that's my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 30, Ifeta Kurspahic, approximately 17 years old. Do you believe a person by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 31, Igabala Kurspahic, approximately 58 years old. Do you believe a person by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 32, Ismet Kurspahic, approximately 3 years old. Do you believe a person by that name, a child by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 33, Ismeta Kurspahic, approximately 26 years old. Do you believe a person by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 34, Izeta Kurspahic, approximately 24 years old. Do you believe a person by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. This name Izeta is unfamiliar to me. Maybe it's under another name. Maybe that person is under another name. We'll see as we go along the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Very well. Number 35, Kada Kurspahic, approximately 40 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: The first name is right, but the last name is Sehic. It's only the maiden name that's Kurspahic. That's my sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So your sister is referred to later at number 67, isn't she, under the name Kada Sehic.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I just want to ask you specifically about the name Kada Kurspahic at number 35, approximately 40 years old. Do you or have you - think about it, please - have you ever known a Kada Kurspahic other than your sister, her maiden name?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. So do you believe that a person called Kada Kurspahic, of that surname perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And number 36 is Latifa Kurspahic, approximately 23 years old. Do you believe a person by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 37, Lejla, L-a-j-l-a [sic], Kurspahic, approximately 4 years old. Do you believe she perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. Let me check on my list. Maybe it's Latifa's daughter or Enis's daughter. Let me check, if you can give me a second. I don't have the name. This is Latifa's daughter, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. So is your answer that you don't believe this person perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: She didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 38, Maida, M-a-i-d-a, Kurspahic, age is unknown. She was a little girl. Do you believe a little girl by this name perished in the Pionirska fire? And if you don't know at any stage, please say so.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 39, Medina, M-e-d-i-n-a, Kurspahic, approximately 28 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Just going back briefly to Maida Kurspahic. If she was the -- if she was the daughter of Dzehva, D-z-e-h-v-a, who's now deceased, would that assist you with your answer to that entry?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that sounds like counsel testifying to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you able to assist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Very well. Number 40, Medo Kurspahic, approximately 50 years old. Do you believe that person perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 41, Mejra, M-e-j-r-a, Kurspahic, approximately 47 years old. Do you believe that person perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 42, Meva, M-e-v-a, Kurspahic, approximately 45 years old. Do you believe that person perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you see a person called Meva Kurspahic at any time since the Pionirska fire in 1992?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. She died after the war in Sarajevo. She spent a period of time in Austria as a refugee.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And when did you last see her?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Roughly three years ago. I don't know. I was supposed to visit her when she was taken ill, and she was with her daughter in Sarajevo, and I was -- I attended the funeral. I think it was three years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What year would this Meva have been born?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Between 45 and 50 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: 45 or 50 years of age when? Do you mean at the time of the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And is this the same spelling of the person that you saw three years ago or who died three years ago, M-e-v-a?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: With Meva, are you able to give us her parents' names?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I know that her father's name is Bego and that she was born in the village of Zlijeb, Visegrad municipality. I don't know anything else. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 43, Mina Kurspahic, approximately 20 years old. Do you believe that she perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 44, Mirela, M-i-r-e-l-a, approximately 3 years old in 1992. Do you believe that she perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 45, Mujesira, M-u-j-e-s-i-r-a, Kurspahic, approximately 35 years old. Do you believe she perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 46, Munevera, M-u-n-e-v-e-r-a, Kurspahic, approximately 20 years old. Do you believe that she perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 47, Munira, M-u-n-i-r-a, Kurspahic, approximately 12 years old. Do you believe she perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Munira is 15. She could not have been 12. That's an error, and she perished, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So you're saying Munira Kurspahic who perished in the fire was, in fact, 15 years old.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter said 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... something, 52, I believe he said, but I believe that's the next one on the list. There's two Muniras. Counsel has to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Witness, there were two Muniras Kurspahics. One listed as 12 and one listed as 55 on the list. I'm going to ask you again about number 47, Munira Kurspahic. What was the age of the Munira Kurspahic, the young girl who perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know about Munira. I can see Munira appearing twice. The one under 48 did perish.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Munira Kurspahic, number 48, approximately 55 years old. You say she did perish in your belief in the Pionirska fire.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. I need go back to 47 just to clarify that, please. Number 47 is Munira Kurspahic, which says approximately 12 years old. Was there a young Munira Kurspahic, a girl, who perished in the Pionirska fire and --

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Does it assist if the -- all right. All right. I'm moving on to number 49, Osman Kurspahic, approximately 67 years old. Do you believe a person by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 50, Kurspahic - and please forgive me if you've been asked before, but I'm going through the list, so we have to ask again - Kurspahic, it gives alternative first names, Pasana or Pasija, approximately 56 years old. Was a person by that name or one of those names, is it your belief that person perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, and her name is Pasija, not Pasana.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could you please spell that.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: P-a-s-i-j-a, Pasija.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 51 is Ramiza Kurspahic, approximately 57 years old. Do you believe a person by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: 52, Sabiha, S-a-b-i-h-a, Kurspahic, approximately 14 years old. Do you believe a person by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 53, Sadeta, S-a-d-e-t-a, Kurspahic, approximately 18 years old. Do you believe a person by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 54, Safa, S-a-f-a, Kurspahic, approximately 50 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 55, Saha or Saha, S-a-h-a, Kurspahic, approximately 70 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you -- have you ever seen a Saha Kurspahic since the date of the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. She survived and lived in Sarajevo. She died in Sarajevo and is buried at the city cemetery. I attended her funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. Are you able to give us any of her relatives, the lady you saw alive, her parents, brothers and sisters, or children.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Parents' names?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. She was native of Klasnik, the village next to Lukic where Milan and Sredoje hail from. I don't know the name of her parents. She was an elderly lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Do you know the names of any of her siblings?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I do. One of her brothers is Sulejman, and the other, Imzo. The third one lived in Visegrad, and he, too, died. I don't remember his name. She had a son, Safet, and four daughters. She lived next-door to my mother's house where I was born and lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And other than the lady you're describing now, do you know any other women, or have you ever known any other women with the first name of Saha or Saha?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And finally on that, the spelling, is it S-a-h-a, as you see before, or is it a capital S with the small accent on the top?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: S with a diacritic, S-a-h-a, Saha.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Number 56, Sajma, S-a-j-m-a, Kurspahic, approximately 20 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. But Sajmija, S-a-j-m-i-j-a, is her full name, whereas Sajma is her nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, if you need to correct any of the others as we move to the end of the list in terms of spelling, please indicate that. Number 57, Seila, S-e-i-l-a, Kurspahic, approximately 2 years old. Do you believe this young child perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, but her name is Sejla, S with a diacritic, not an S, but a Sh, Seila.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Number 58, and this is possibly Seniha, S-e-n-i-h-a, approximately 9 years old. Do you believe a person -- a child by that name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, but her name is Seniha.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. Number 59, Sumbula, S-u-m-b-u-l-a, Kurspahic, approximately 62 years old. Did a person by this name in your belief perish in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 60, Vahid Kurspahic, V-a-h-i-d, approximately 8 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 61, Fazila Memisevic, F-a-z-i-l-a, Memisevic, approximately 54 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 62, Redzo, R-e-d-z-o, Memisevic, approximately 57 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 63, Rabija Sadikovic, R-a-b-i-j-a, Sadikovic, approximately 52 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, number 64 is Enver Sehic, approximately 13 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No. Lukic took his father and him together with others out of the house. He did not perish in Pionirska. He was taken away and disappeared without trace.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And did that occur before the Pionirska fire incident or after it?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Before.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, are you aware of any other persons by name of Enver Sehic, other than your nephew?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I don't know. He's my sister's -- my sister Kada's son. I don't know any other Emir [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: You don't know any other Enver, E-n-v-e-r, Sehics, other than your nephew.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, number 65, Faruk Sehic, approximately 12 years old. Is that your nephew?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And do you believe that he perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 66, Haraga, H-a-r-a-g-a, Haraga Sehic, age unknown. First I need to ask you, do you recognise the name Haraga as being male or female?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Haraga should be a male; Hajrija should be a female. But I don't know this person. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So you don't know any Haraga Sehic -- you don't believe that number 66, Haraga Sehic, perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And was it your testimony that you don't know anyone by this name as it's spelt here?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: I knew a man by that name, Haraga Sehic from the village of Mala Gostilje, who died before the war, and he's the only one by that name I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 67, Kada Sehic, approximately 39 years old. That is your sister who perished in the Pionirska fire.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 68, Nurka Velic, N-u-r-k-a, approximately 70 years old. Do you believe this person perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes, but it's not an N, Nurka. It's an M, M-u-r-k-a. Murka.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 69, Tima Velic, T-i-m-a, approximately 35 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Number 70, Jasmina Vila, approximately 20 years old. Do you believe a person by this name perished in the Pionirska fire?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Mr. Kurspahic, we've been through the 70 names on this list, one by one. Now, in addition to those 70 names, what other names, what other victims' names, and if you need to consult your list, please do so, what other names of persons who have not been referred to on the list I've put to you, what other names do you believe are victims of the Pionirska fire in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, we would object, for unscheduled victims now being brought in by the backdoor at the very eleventh hour of these proceedings. This is a case without precedent, to have that kind of attempt by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, what do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: In fairness to the witness, sir, he's brought along a list today. He's testified to the Court that -- as to the source of the information in his list. He's referred to that list with that information as he -- we've gone through each of the victims in the indictment; and it would be unfair to the witness who's compiled this list if he's only able to give half his testimony effectively, the ones that we've asked him about, when he has a rich source, it seems, of information not only on the victims we have here but on some others. Counsel's entitled to cross-examine him in due course, but in fairness, I think, sir, he should -- Your Honour, should be able to relate those other names to the Court now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would add that the Court needs to be concerned about the fairness of the proceedings and the fairness of my client in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence and the statute of the Tribunal and what they require for notice of elements that needs to be proven by the Prosecution and the case he needs to -- or that he would need to rebut and address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you seeking to amend the indictment to include any names that the witness might add?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I just had my instruction that we're not intending to do that, to add any further names. It's come up --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any other names to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is a matter for the Chamber, Witness, not for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, in fact, sir, he just indicated he didn't have any further names to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. I didn't hear. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: He's obviously put that time to good use, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So the answer to that last question just confirming that, there are no names on your list that I haven't asked you about.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If I could just have a moment, Your Honour. Oh, yes, there was one matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Earlier in your testimony, Mr. Kurspahic, you had a -- maybe a newspaper clipping or something else similar to that that you held up when you were being asked questions by counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seriously object to this. This is an article based upon the video-tape that you did not permit me to introduce into evidence, so I would strenuously object on that ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Counsel knows more than I do, Your Honour. I haven't seen it, and I don't know what it is. If it's a newspaper item, perhaps I can just ask the witness what it is and we can take it from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, find out what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Please don't read from it, Mr. Kurspahic, but what is that copy of a newspaper article that you brought with you?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: The last time we went up to our village where our people were driven out from, the lad whose wife and small infant were burned gave a statement, and I'm sure that the gentlemen can read this quite well, and I can give it to them. I think they hail from the region and know the language, and none of what I brought along is a secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, I have one matter here. Do you recall during your earlier testimony, Mr. Kurspahic, you were shown a document about Mr. Redzo Memisevic requesting, I think, some property to be returned?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: This document is not accurate, and I state this upon my full responsibility. The man is not alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So I think the gist of your response to counsel was that members of a deceased person's family can make a request on the name of the deceased person. Does that summarise your answer?

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And that's your understanding. It was the family of Redzo Memisevic making the request on his name.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: His son. His son must have done it, Ibrahim, or actually his real name is Asim. To tell you the truth, back where I come from we all had two names or nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you confirm your earlier testimony that Redzo Memisevic perished in the Pionirska fire.

utterances.speaker: HUSO KURSPAHIC.
utterances.text: Yes. We've already written that down.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
