utterances.text: Mr. ... did you have something to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would apply -- there was a portion of the trip that was in closed session by error. That would be page 41, line 7 through transcript page 53, line 7. I would ask that that should be reclassified as public as there is no sensitive information contained therein, and the right to a public trial is of paramount concern, especially given the critical matters that were discussed, the very important matters that were discussed in that portion of today's transcript, and I was told that I need to make an application, so I do so now while it's still fresh in everyone's mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You want to have that in public session?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. It was inadvertently left in private session, and then I believe at some point in time while Mr. Cole was doing his examination, it was realised and it was then in public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have the Registrar confirm what you have said, Mr. Ivetic, and give the ruling later. Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't need that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just make sure that we have that -- the list that he brought with him, is it in the custody of the Court now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The list -- just a minute, Witness. Do we have the list -- please return to your seat. May we have the list that you had prepared along with members of your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have left a copy, and I can leave this with you. I don't need it. The list is identical. I also gave a copy to the Defence, and it's one and the same list that allowed me to go through all the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For the record, we are shown one by the usher, and I believe it was taken, so I do not have a copy. I don't know whether that's -- I believe that it had already been tendered by Mr. Cole into -- as a potential exhibit, and he'd marked it for identification, so it should also be in the pile, I would imagine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we had marked it for identification, did we?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... it appears to be the one -- that I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have two decisions to give. On the 3rd of November, 2008, the Trial Chamber determined that Dr. Wil Fagel's testimony will only become relevant if and when certain documents here referred to as the Defence documents are introduced by the Defence of Milan Lukic in support of its Defence of alibi. On the 25th of March, 2009, the Trial Chamber affirmed that Dr. Fagel could testify as an alibi rebuttal witness and limited his testimony to the Defence documents and a particular hand-drawn map, but only to the extent that such documents are admitted into evidence. Dr. Fagel is scheduled to testify on Wednesday. That's tomorrow. One of the Defence documents was introduced by the Milan Lukic Defence on the 1st of September, 2008. And it is Exhibit 1D25.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On the 3rd of April, the Prosecution rebuttal witness, Stoja Vujicic, was specifically asked questions concerning the authenticity of the Defence documents. Upon the Prosecution's request, four of the documents were admitted as P320, 321, 322, and 323. The hand-drawn map has not been tendered into evidence by any party. At the time the Prosecution tendered the four documents into evidence, the Milan Lukic Defence noted for the record that in line with the Trial Chamber's 3rd November, 2008, decision, these documents could not be the basis for calling Dr. Fagel. The Prosecution did not comment on the submissions. All but one of the Defence documents have been introduced into evidence by the Prosecution. In the Trial Chamber's opinion, therefore, Dr. Fagel could only testify about Exhibit 1D25, the one document which is properly tendered by the Defence of Milan Lukic in support of the Defence of alibi. The Chamber, therefore, holds that it is not in the interest of judicial economy at this point in the proceedings to have Dr. Fagel testify. However, the Prosecution may tender into evidence the relevant part of Dr. Fagel's report, which concerns 1D25. I proceed to the next decision: On the 3rd of April, the Chamber granted the Prosecution's request to remove VG-145 from its list of rebuttal witnesses. Today, the Prosecution requested once more to add VG-145 as a rebuttal witness. The Defence of Milan Lukic stated in response that Mr. Alarid had prepared to cross-examine VG-145 and that he's out of the country. In the Defence view, it would be improper for Mr. Ivetic to examine VG-145 in light of the serious allegations the Prosecution raised. The Chamber notes that it has heard one of the three witnesses whom the Prosecution sought to bring following the Chamber's oral decision on 13th March, 2009; that is VG-146. In that decision, the Chamber stated that the allegations made by the Prosecution in its motion for contempt raised, and here I quote, "a question as to whether the evidence that the Chamber has heard from MLD1 and might hear from VG-145 and others is reliable, and its impact if any on the Chamber's assessment on the evidence in the proceedings as a whole." For these reasons and considering the stage of the proceedings, the evidence on the record which is potentially affected and that the Prosecution has called VG-146, the Chamber is not persuaded that it is necessary to hear VG-145, and the Prosecution's request is therefore denied. That's the end of the second decision.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next decision. On the 2nd of April, the Defence of Milan Lukic filed a motion requesting that the deadline for the final briefs be moved to Monday, the 11th of May, and that closing arguments be held in the week of 18th of May. It also requested each party be allotted 180 to 240 minutes for closing arguments. The Prosecution responded on the 3rd of April, disputing the allegations made by the Defence motion, and requests that the Chamber order that all final trial briefs are to be submitted simultaneously. The Prosecution states that it defers to the Chamber regarding matters of scheduling. The Chamber has considered the submissions and notes that several of the Defence arguments have been raised in past extension requests, several of which the Chamber has granted. But the Chamber is sensitive to the Defence situation, particularly in light of the fact that Mr. Alarid as lead counsel is absent. The Chamber, therefore, orders that all parties are to file their final briefs by Wednesday, 22nd April, 4.00 p.m., and closing arguments are to be presented Monday, 27th April, at a time and in a courtroom to be announced. But the Chamber does not see any reason at this point to vary the time previously allotted to each party for presenting the final submissions. The Chamber considers that this also disposes of the request of the Defence in its third notice, filed on 2nd April, for a pause in the proceedings to permit further verification of the indictment's list of victims of the Pionirska Street incident. End of that decision. Next one: On the 2nd of April, the Defence of Milan Lukic filed a motion with several requests in relation to Witness CW1, whose testimony claims calls into question the list of alleged victims of the Pionirska Street incident. The Defence has presented evidence to the effect that three persons listed as deceased in Annex A of the indictment are alive and by which it seeks to cast doubt on the status of several other persons listed in Annex A. However, the fact that three persons may have been confirmed alive does not warrant the automatic dismissal of counts in the indictment. Any issues raised by such evidence are more properly considered during the Chamber's deliberations. The Defence request in this regard is therefore denied. Also denied is the request that the trial be declared a mistrial. Finally, the Defence requests that all of the Prosecution's witnesses for the Pionirska Street incident be recalled to testify. Such a course of action would, however, be contrary to the interests of judicial economy at this advanced stage of the proceedings. The Chamber has accommodated the Defence by permitting Huso Kurspahic to be called as a Chamber witness in light of new information provided by him concerning victims of the Pionirska Street incident. Without any similar information from other Prosecution witnesses, the Chamber cannot see the merit in the Defence request, which is consequently denied. The Chamber considers that this decision also disposes of the remaining requests from the third notice as to named murder victims in the indictment for whom evidence exists that they're alive, filed on the 2nd of April, 2009. End of decision. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to address the Chamber on its first decision and just remind the Chamber of the procedural history, and perhaps the Chamber would reconsider its decision. With respect to Dr. Fagel's report, if the Chamber recalls, the reason -- well, the documents were given to the Prosecution in support of the alibi. It was because the Chamber had required us to submit or present our rebuttal case in our case in chief that we were required to disclose his findings with respect to those documents prior to them being tendered. One was tendered prior to that report, and then the report was disclosed, and then the other documents weren't tendered. I submit, Your Honour, that since they were provided to the Prosecution by an officer of the Court with the representation that they were going -- they supported the alibi that the Prosecution shouldn't be denied the ability to introduce evidence in light -- in view -- in the form of Dr. Fagel showing that they are, in fact, forged documents. They're also, Your Honour, the one document that was introduced is inextricably linked to the other documents in that Dr. Fagel's opinion is based on the fact that all of the signatures on the documents are carbon copies or digital copies. They're exactly the same. He's unable to say that if it's just talking about the single isolated document. And then with respect to the map, Your Honour, except your decision with respect to VG-145, the person that we intended to introduce that, but discussing it with some colleagues last evening, I think there's an alternative theory upon which the map could be introduced through Dr. Fagel. Someone reminded me yesterday evening that the conviction in the Charles Lindbergh case was based on an handwriting expert saying that the ransom note was -- the hand was written by the hand of the particular accused in that case. I believe that we could establish the foundation of the map and its attribution to Mr. Milan Lukic through Dr. Fagel. It does contain information about what happened at the Drina that only a person, I believe, who was present at the Drina could provide, so it would be my submission, Your Honour, that if the Chamber credits Dr. Fagel's evidence with respect to who drafted the map that the Chamber would be entitled to admit the exhibit into evidence. And Your Honour, just one other -- sorry, and then I'm finished for the day. One other thing. If we're not permitted to call Dr. Fagel, I would just ask if we get a later start for VG-94. She arrives late this evening, and we'll not be able to speak with her this evening. If we could just have an hour in the morning just to see what her state of mind is like and prepare her for her testimony tomorrow. I'd appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The first mart is essentially a request for reconsideration, so I wanted to hear from Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, with respect to Dr. Fagel, the parties have been operating based upon the Trial Chamber's ruling of -- I forget if it was 8th or 4th November, stating that if the Defence introduced documents, Mr. Fagel would be permitted to testify. We did not introduce those documents. The Prosecution cannot introduce its own controversy into the case then ask its own expert to opine on the controversy. There's one very simple explanation for the document that apparently counsel nor Dr. Fagel have considered, and we would be making that in our submissions, since it appears he is not appearing, so we will not be cross-examining on the topic. Your Honours have ruled, rightly so, I think, with respect to the history of the case and the manner on which those documents came in. We brought live witnesses who testified as to the alibis, and Your Honours can consider those live witnesses and make the appropriate findings, and I think that -- I would strongly oppose reconsideration, and I think that the order should stand. It's in line with the Court's prior decision and the course of practice of how the parties operated was under that prior order. So if we're now changing the prior order, then obviously persons might have done things a little differently. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the Chamber's view, it hasn't heard anything from the Prosecutor that would warrant reconsideration in the interests of justice, and we haven't heard any new material being presented, so the Chamber will not grant the request for reconsideration. We'll start at 10.00 tomorrow morning.
